result.result:
The app is built and working. `npx @angular/cli@19 serve` starts it, and logging in with `admin` / `admin` reaches the dashboard. I ran the whole flow in a headless browser at 1280px:

- **Login:** submitting empty fields shows the error states.
- **Navigation:** the dashboard and users pages load from the header links.
- **Profile menu:** it opens leftward and stays inside the viewport (right edge at 1256px). Clicking outside closes it, and Sign Out returns to `/login`.
- **Users:** all four dialogs open and close. Edit, invite and delete each go through the in-memory API, and the table updates after each one. The delete confirmation also closes on a backdrop click.
- **Console:** no errors or warnings.

That test caught one bug, now fixed: the open profile menu was drawn underneath the "Invite Member" button.

**What it's built from.** Every screen uses the dsb components: header, footer, inputs, checkbox, dropdown, buttons, tags, avatar, list, table and modal. Styles use only `--ds-decisions-*` tokens. A search of `src/` finds no hex or rgb colours and no tier-1 or tier-3 tokens.

**Where Figma and the spec disagreed, I followed the spec's wording and Figma's layout:**
- **Text:** Figma shows "Sign in to your account", different numbers and different service names. I used the spec's text. I left out the brand title and the divider on the login card because the spec says to add nothing else.
- **Users table:** Figma combines avatar and name into one "User" column; I kept them as separate columns, as the spec lists them. Role badges follow Figma: Admin red, Editor blue, Viewer grey.
- **Dashboard order:** Figma puts Service Health before the chart and has only six cards. The spec lists eight tiles in a different order. I used a 12-column grid: four metric tiles; then Throughput and Service Health; then Data Summary and System Logs. That means System Logs is not full width as in Figma, and Figma's "System Overview" heading isn't there.
- **Header nav:** Figma's links (Overview, Metrics, Logs, Settings) don't lead anywhere, so the nav is Dashboard and Users. Figma's "Online" badge in the header isn't shown, and the dsb footer brings link columns that Figma's single-row footer doesn't have.

**Where the design system couldn't express the design:**
- **Fonts:** there's no font-family token. I set Inter (the Figma font) globally and a monospace font for the log viewer. These are the only font literals.
- **Sizes:** the largest font size is 22px, so the 26px tile values render at 22px. The largest corner radius is 10px, so the 12px login card corners are 10px. There's no card-shadow token, so the tiles have none.
- **Heights:** there's no token for the chart or log viewer height, so both are multiples of the spacing token `space-7xl`.
- **Breakpoints:** the two responsive breakpoints are plain pixel values, because CSS variables can't be used in media queries.
- **Header and modal slots:**
  - The dsb header has no slot for a user menu, so the profile menu is positioned over its right edge.
  - The header's links are plain anchors, which would reload the page and wipe the mock data. Clicks are routed through Angular instead.
  - The modal has no setting for Figma's divider lines above and below the dialog body, so those aren't there.
- **Avatar fallback:** the avatar falls back to initials only when it gets no image URL, not when an image fails to load. The users page tests each image and passes no URL for any that fail.

**Setup changes.** The project folder only had the two dsb packages, so I generated an Angular 19 app with the CLI and merged it in. The packages that came pre-installed were Angular 21 and wouldn't resolve against 19, so I deleted `node_modules` and the lockfile and reinstalled. I also removed the Karma test setup the generator adds by default.
